claims.text: A tungsten-doped diamond-like carbon coating will be deposited by PVD onto the CoCrFeNi matrix.
The WDLC coating will maintain a stable low-friction, low-wear interface from approximately 25 °C to 800 °C.
The amorphous carbon structure of WDLC provides low friction at room temperature.
Tungsten doping promotes retention of the low-friction DLC structure at low temperatures.
Tungsten doping enhances the high-temperature chemical stability of the DLC coating up to 800 °C.
Tungsten in the coating forms stable tungsten oxide species at high temperature.
Protective oxide phases can inhibit continued oxidation and contribute to favorable high-temperature tribological behavior.
The tungsten-derived oxide phases will maintain a load-bearing, low-shear interface on WDLC-coated CoCrFeNi.
High-temperature sliding can soften metallic surfaces and promote oxidation, adhesion, delamination, and increased wear.
Bare CoCrFeNi specifically exhibits increasing friction and wear at elevated temperatures because of oxidation and surface softening.
The unmodified CoCrFeNi surface lacks a protective tribochemical layer.
WDLC-coated CoCrFeNi will have a substantially lower coefficient of friction than bare CoCrFeNi throughout the 25–800 °C range.
WDLC-coated CoCrFeNi will have a reduced wear rate relative to bare CoCrFeNi throughout the 25–800 °C range.
The WDLC coating will improve surface-layer durability under both low- and high-temperature sliding.
The predicted benefit applies in oxidizing environments under normal loads up to approximately 30 N.
The exact quantitative reductions in friction and wear remain unknown.
Long-term coating adhesion and stability under cyclic thermal and mechanical stress remain unverified.
Failure to obtain statistically significant reductions in both friction and wear across the full temperature range, or severe degradation at any tested temperature, will falsify the hypothesis.
